issues.description: ACL root check uses HasParent without explicit handling of equality and nil-namespace cases
issues.detail: In vault/acl.go AllowOperation, the new root check reads: if !ns.HasParent(a.root) { return ret }. This silently conflates two distinct preconditions: (1) ns == a.root (the policy is being evaluated in its own namespace) and (2) ns is a strict descendant of a.root. The semantics of HasParent are not stated alongside the call, and there is no invariant comment establishing whether HasParent returns true for the identity case. If HasParent is strict-ancestor-only, then a root token issued in namespace N is denied in N itself, which is wrong; if it is non-strict, the comment ('parent (ancestor)') is misleading. Either way, the author has not stated the precondition (what does HasParent mean here?) nor the postcondition (which ns values must yield Allowed=true). State the spec, or refuse.

issues.description: NamespaceSealed is a stub that unconditionally returns false and is already wired into security-relevant call sites
issues.detail: vault/core.go introduces (*Core).NamespaceSealed returning false with a TODO. The PR description states ListAllNamespaces now includes sealed namespaces 'currently stubbed with NamespaceSealed stub'. This is the textbook DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE / TESTED-NOT-PROVED antipattern dressed as scaffolding: a predicate central to access-control safety is committed in a state where it cannot, by construction, return its intended value. There is no compile-time guarantee that downstream code will be updated when SealManager lands, and no test can ever prove the negative path because the function has no negative path. Either gate it behind a build tag or interface so the unimplemented branch is unreachable, or do not merge until SealManager exists.

issues.description: Error-classification refactor in AdjustErrorStatusCode silently changes precedence among matching conditions
issues.detail: sdk/logical/response_util.go previously evaluated each error class with independent if-statements, so multiple status assignments could occur in declared order with the last write winning. The refactor to a switch with the first matching case wins reverses this for any err that matches more than one predicate (e.g. an HTTPCodedError wrapping ErrSealed). The author has not stated the invariant the function maintains over the set of errors that satisfy multiple branches, nor demonstrated that no production error path matches more than one. This is a behavioural change disguised as a stylistic cleanup.

issues.description: Loss of root-namespace invariant in NewACL has no compensating check at policy attachment time
issues.detail: Previously NewACL refused a root-named policy outside the root namespace ('root policy is only allowed in root namespace'). The new code accepts it and stores ns as a.root. The system-wide invariant 'the only authority that can grant root privileges is the root namespace' has been replaced by 'whatever namespace was in context when NewACL was called'. Whether that is safe depends entirely on every caller of NewACL having validated that the requesting principal is authorized to mint a root policy at that ns. The PR does not exhibit that proof, and the call sites are not in the diff. Either show the invariant is preserved across all NewACL callers, or restore the guard.

issues.description: Reordering of namespace lookup before path-traversal guard changes failure mode
issues.detail: AllowOperation previously consulted a.root before namespace.FromContext; now FromContext is called first and a context with no namespace yields an empty ACLResults (default deny) before the root fast-path can fire. For root tokens this is safe; for the previous semantics where root was a pure 'if a.root then allow' check regardless of context, it is a tightening. The change may be intended, but no specification of the new behaviour is given, and the function's contract on a missing-namespace context is now silently 'deny' rather than 'allow if root, else deny'. State the contract.

issues.description: Substitution of namespaceMountEntryView with NamespaceView(c.barrier, ns).SubView removes a root-namespace special case without documenting equivalence
issues.detail: vault/expiration.go previously branched on ns.ID == RootNamespaceID, using systemBarrierView for root and namespaceMountEntryView otherwise. The replacement unifies both into NamespaceView(...).SubView(...). For this to be a refactor rather than a behavioural change, NamespaceView(barrier, RootNamespace).SubView(p) must produce a view over the exact same byte range as systemBarrierView.SubView(p) stripped of the root prefix. No comment, assertion, or test asserts this equivalence. A one-line invariant comment or a migration test would discharge the obligation; absent that, this is a TESTED-NOT-PROVED claim.

issues.description: Comment for ACL.root field is grammatically and semantically imprecise
issues.detail: The new comment reads: 'root property is a non-nil namespace if the "root" named policy (and only "root") is present.' The field is a *namespace.Namespace, not 'a non-nil namespace', and the parenthetical condition '(and only "root")' is not reflected in the type. A precise comment would state: 'root is non-nil iff the policy set consists of exactly one policy named "root"; when non-nil it identifies the namespace in which that policy was instantiated.' Prose should match the invariant the code maintains; this prose does not.

issues.description: Token length constant NSTokenLength = TokenLen + "."[1] + nsID is described arithmetically but is a string concatenation in intent
issues.detail: The PR description specifies NSTokenLength as '(TokenLen + "."[1] + nsID)'. As written this is the sum of an integer, a byte (the ASCII value of '.', i.e. 46), and an nsID — not a token-length formula. If the intended meaning is len(TokenLen) + 1 + len(nsID), say so. If the constant is a number, give the units. The reader should not have to guess whether '.' is a separator or a numeric contribution. State the spec.

review.summary: REFUSED as written, on grounds of UNREASONED preconditions and TESTED-NOT-PROVED scaffolding. Two findings are load-bearing: (1) NamespaceSealed is a stub that returns false unconditionally and is already wired into security-adjacent paths — a predicate whose negative branch cannot be exercised should not be merged into a security boundary, even with a TODO; (2) the ACL root-policy check has been weakened from 'root policy only in root namespace' to 'root policy in any namespace, scoped by HasParent', and neither the semantics of HasParent for the identity case nor the invariants preserved across NewACL callers are stated in the diff. The response_util switch-refactor silently changes precedence for errors matching multiple predicates. The expiration view unification is plausibly a true refactor but ships without the equivalence assertion that would let a reader verify it without simulating both code paths in their head. State the precondition, the postcondition, and the invariant for each of these, or do not merge.
